correctness.rationale: For complete multipartite K_(n_1,...,n_r) with all parts nonempty, r>=2 and minimum degree>=2, every colour appears in at most half each open neighbourhood. With two colours, each part sign sum S_i must equal global S, hence all S_i=0 and all n_i even. K4 and K_(1,1,2) force four distinct colours. Adding two differently coloured vertices to any fixed part increases each other open neighbourhood count by <=1 while degree grows by 2; preserves 3-colour validity. Reducing each part modulo 2 to size1 or2, plus handling parity core K4/K112 by first restoring one pair, gives explicitly coloured n=3,5,6,7, n>=8 and three enlarged n=6 cores, exhausting all cases. Independent brute force checked exact 2- and 3-colour minima for all 51 admissible unlabeled profiles of orders 3..8; official 9246 profiles through 25 checked constructively, neither finite set used to establish general proof.
residual_risks: No claim at minimum degree one (no colouring), with list constraints, or for unrelated graph majority-colouring definitions.
